## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The presentations and parameters of the Statement.

[F1] The arbitrary monic cyclotomic Hecke quotients are finite-dimensional by
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-bounded-ordered-monomials-span]]. Their mixed and
quadratic relations are those of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]].

[F2] In the KLR presentation, a crossing between distant colors has square
$1$ and interchanges their word idempotents
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]).
On any finite color interval, homogeneous cyclotomic content algebras are
finite-dimensional with nilpotent dots
([[lem-cyclotomic-klr-dot-annihilators-and-finite-root-strings]]).

## Proof

1.1 Work over a finite splitting extension for the finitely many minimal polynomials of the commuting polynomial generators in the finite regular module of [F1]. Simultaneous primary decomposition gives joint generalized eigenspaces. On such a weight, the first value is a charge root, because the first cyclotomic polynomial annihilates the module. In the degenerate case connect distinct values differing by $1$; in the nondegenerate case connect distinct nonzero values whose ratio is $\xi$ or $\xi^{-1}$. This defines a graph on the distinct values in each word, with at most $d$ vertices. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 For a KLR word, form the induced line graph on its distinct colors. If a component contains no charge, move its first occurrence left across all earlier letters. These letters lie in other components, so their color differences exceed $1$; [F2] makes every crossing invertible. The resulting word idempotent is nonzero if the original was, but its first color has exponent zero, so the cyclotomic relation kills it. This contradiction shows that each component contains a charge. A component with at most $d$ vertices is an interval, and every color has distance at most $d-1$ from a charge in that component. [F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The mixed relations give intertwiners $\theta_r=s_r(x_r-x_{r+1})+1$ and $\Theta_r=T_r(1-X_rX_{r+1}^{-1})+1-\xi$. Direct multiplication gives $\theta_r^2=1-(x_r-x_{r+1})^2$ and $\Theta_r^2=(1-\xi X_{r+1}X_r^{-1})(1-\xi X_rX_{r+1}^{-1})$; they interchange the two polynomial generators and commute with the others. For example $s_r(x_r-x_{r+1})=-(x_r-x_{r+1})s_r-2$, which yields the first square identity; the second follows by inserting $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ and $T_rX_rT_r=\xi X_{r+1}$. Between values in different graph components these squares have nonzero constant terms, hence are invertible on the generalized weight space. Each intertwiner therefore gives an isomorphism onto the swapped generalized weight space. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Suppose a component contains no charge root. Its earliest occurrence in the word can be moved to the first position by the invertible swaps of step 2.1: every preceding value belongs to a different component. The resulting nonzero weight space has an uncharged first value, contradicting the first cyclotomic relation. Consequently each component contains a charge root. A simple path from that root to any vertex has length at most $d-1$, so the value is an integer within $d-1$ of an integral charge, respectively a power $\xi^a$ with $|a-m_j|\le d-1$. Infinite order of $\xi$ makes the integer labels unique. All spectral values therefore belong to $k$, and their polynomial primary projectors descend to $k$ by the Chinese remainder identity. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Only finitely many words satisfy this bound. In every content presentation the generators and relations use only colors already present in that content, so replacing the full line by a finite interval containing the bound changes none of these presentations. All omitted contents have zero word idempotents by step 1.2. On the finite interval [F2] supplies finite-dimensionality and nilpotent dots, and the finite sum is finite-dimensional. This identifies the full rank algebra with each sufficiently large finite window, including compatibility of larger windows on the same generators. At level zero the first exponent is always zero, killing every positive-rank word; the Hecke polynomial is $1$ and gives the same zero quotient. Rank zero is the ground field by definition. No basis correspondence or Hecke--KLR inverse map has been used. [step 3.1, step 1.2, F1, F2, given] ∎

Replacing $\tau$ by $-\psi$ gives $\psi u-v\psi=-1$, $\psi v-u\psi=1$, and $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1-\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2=[Q(u,v)-Q(w,v)]/(w-u)$ on colors $(a,b,a)$.

[F2] The degenerate affine Hecke generator presentation of [[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] over $\mathbb C$ has the relations listed in the Statement; here that presentation defines the algebra over $k$, and its basis and faithful action are proved below. The generators $s_r$ permute positions; the distinct notation $\sigma_r$ below means actual permutation operators on polynomial or formal coefficient functions.

## Proof

**Given:** The data and conventions of the Statement, and [F1]–[F2].

1.1 The coefficient completions. A symmetric polynomial in the commuting $x$ is central: the mixed relation gives $s_rf=(\sigma_rf)s_r-(f-\sigma_rf)/(x_r-x_{r+1})$, first on monomials by induction, then on polynomials. A symmetric $f$ has zero correction. The fiber of the elementary symmetric polynomials over their values on $\beta$ consists exactly of the ordered permutations of $\beta$: the coordinates are roots with multiplicities of $\prod_{a\in\beta}(t-a)$. Its radical is the intersection of the finitely many corresponding maximal ideals, by the polynomial factorization and the fact that every coordinate satisfies this monic polynomial. The elementary-symmetric ideal and this radical have cofinal powers, since the fiber is finite dimensional and its radical nilpotent. Chinese remainders and completion therefore give $\mathcal B_\beta$ with local coordinates $x_r-\nu_r$. On the KLR side symmetric dot polynomials are central by [F1], and the same argument at the all-zero fiber shows that its coefficient completion is $\mathcal B_\beta$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Invertible tables. If $a\ne b$ the integer $a-b$ is a nonzero unit in $k$, so $z^{-1}$ exists as a formal geometric series. In the backward case $a=b+1$, $q=z^{-1}$ has constant $1$. In the other unequal cases $q=1-z^{-1}$ has constant $1-(a-b)^{-1}$, which could vanish only when $a-b=1$, already excluded. Equal colors give constant $1$. For unequal colors $p_{ba}(v,u)=-p_{ab}(u,v)$. Direct multiplication gives $q_{ab}(u,v)q_{ba}(v,u)=1-z^{-2}$ on nonadjacent colors; on a forward arrow it gives $-(z-1)/z^2=(1-z^{-2})/(v-u)$ since $z=-1+u-v$; on a backward arrow it gives $(z+1)/z^2=(1-z^{-2})/(u-v)$ since $z=1+u-v$. Thus $Q_{ab}q_{ab}\sigma(q_{ba})=1-p_{ab}^2$ in all unequal cases, with no division by a nonunit left unresolved. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 A concrete KLR action. On $\mathcal B_\beta$, dots multiply and idempotents project. Define $E_r=(\sigma_r-1)/(y_r-y_{r+1})$ on equal adjacent colors. The numerator is divisible by the denominator for polynomials and formal series, so $E_r$ preserves the coefficient algebra. For unequal source colors $(a,b)$ define $\psi_r(fe(\nu))=c_{ab}(y_r,y_{r+1})\sigma_r(f)e(s_r\nu)$, where $c_{ab}(u,v)=v-u$ if $a=b+1$ and $c_{ab}(u,v)=1$ otherwise. These explicit operators prove the local relations in the following five cases. [step 2.1, given, construct, algebra]

4.1 Quadratic and dot moves. Write $\delta=u-v$. On equal colors $E^2=0$, since $E(f)$ is invariant under $\sigma$, and $Eu-vE=-1$, $Ev-uE=1$ follow by expanding the numerator. On unequal colors the dot moves are permutation identities and $\psi^2=c_{ba}(u,v)c_{ab}(v,u)=Q_{ab}(u,v)$. Indeed these products are $v-u$ on a forward arrow, $u-v$ on a backward arrow, and $1$ off edges. Disjoint crossings commute because their variables and their two-color factors are disjoint. Idempotent moves and commutative dot relations hold by construction. [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Three distinct colors. Put $u=y_1,v=y_2,w=y_3$, $s=\sigma_1,t=\sigma_2$, $\rho=sts=tst$, $L=\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1$, $M=\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$. On a source $(a,b,c)$ with all colors distinct, direct consecutive application of step 3.1 gives both $L(f)$ and $M(f)$ equal to $c_{bc}(u,v)c_{ac}(u,w)c_{ab}(v,w)\rho(f)$ in the $(c,b,a)$ summand. The three pair factors commute. Hence $L=M$ for every edge pattern among three distinct integer colors. [step 4.1, step 3.1, algebra]

6.1 Exactly the first two equal. On $(a,a,b)$, $a\ne b$, put $h=c_{ab}(u,v)c_{ab}(u,w)$. Consecutive application gives $L(f)=h\,stE_1(f)$ and $M(f)=E_2(h\,stf)$. The polynomial $h$ is symmetric in $v,w$, including the backward case $h=(v-u)(w-u)$, so the product rule $E_2(hg)=E_2(h)g+t(h)E_2(g)$ gives $M(f)=hE_2stf$. Finally $E_2st=stE_1$: both sides equal $(\rho-st)/(v-w)$, with the denominator transformed when the permutation lies to its left. Thus $L=M$. [step 5.1, step 3.1, algebra]

7.1 Exactly the last two equal. On $(a,b,b)$, $a\ne b$, put $h=c_{ab}(u,w)c_{ab}(v,w)$. The two words give $L(f)=E_1(h\,tsf)$ and $M(f)=h\,tsE_2(f)$. Here $h$ is symmetric in $u,v$, including $h=(w-u)(w-v)$ when $a=b+1$. The product rule gives $L(f)=hE_1tsf$. The identity $E_1ts=tsE_2=(\rho-ts)/(u-v)$ now yields $L=M$. This explicitly checks the second repeated-neighbor pattern. [step 6.1, step 3.1, algebra]

8.1 Equal outer colors. On $(a,b,a)$, $a\ne b$, full expansion of the single middle divided difference gives $L(f)=c_{ba}(u,v)[c_{ab}(v,w)\rho(f)-c_{ab}(v,u)f]/(u-w)$ and $M(f)=c_{ab}(v,w)[c_{ba}(u,v)\rho(f)-c_{ba}(w,v)f]/(u-w)$. The $\rho(f)$ terms cancel, and step 4.1 gives $(L-M)(f)=[Q_{ab}(w,v)-Q_{ab}(u,v)]f/(u-w)$. Thus the correction is $+1$ for $a\to b$, $-1$ for $a\leftarrow b$, and zero off edges. The displayed expressions have removable denominators because their original numerators come from divided differences; the final quotient is a polynomial. [step 7.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

9.1 All three equal. For $\Delta=(u-v)(u-w)(v-w)$, expand the three factors $E=(\sigma-1)/(\text{dot difference})$ in either order. Moving permutations to the right gives the complete identity $E_1E_2E_1=E_2E_1E_2=(\rho-st-ts+s+t-1)/\Delta$. For example the $\rho$ coefficient is $1/\Delta$, the $st$ and $ts$ coefficients are $-1/\Delta$, the $s,t$ coefficients are $1/\Delta$, and the identity coefficient is $-1/\Delta$. Both sides preserve formal series by their original divided-difference formulas, so this rational equality proves their equality without inverting dots in the algebra. This supplies the all-equal case omitted in the cited source. [step 8.1, step 3.1, algebra]

10.1 Faithfulness for the KLR action. Moving dots to the right using step 4.1, and replacing repeated crossings and braid differences using steps 5.1–9.1, spans the presented KLR algebra by $\psi_w f(y)e(\nu)$ for fixed reduced words $w$. Termination uses crossing length: every quadratic reduction or braid correction has smaller length; reduced words for a permutation are connected by the elementary symmetric-group braid moves. In the rational-function action each $\psi_w$ has leading term a nonzero coefficient times $w$, and all other terms have smaller permutation length. Distinct permutations of variables are linearly independent over the rational-function field: a shortest putative relation, evaluated on $fg$ minus one selected automorphism's value on $g$ times its evaluation on $f$, gives a shorter nonzero relation. Hence these spanning monomials are independent. The same triangular argument over fractions of formal series proves faithfulness of the completed action, whose elements are the finite sum over $w,\nu$ with formal coefficient $f$. [step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 8.1, step 9.1, algebra]

11.1 Why formal extension is legitimate. There are finitely many $w,\nu$, and each basis vector $\psi_we(\nu)$ has a finite crossing degree. Symmetric positive-degree dots form a central ideal with powers cofinal with dot-degree powers in each coefficient algebra by step 1.1. The PBW module just proved is consequently finite free over its right coefficient algebra and completes coefficientwise. Multiplication extends continuously: moving a formal coefficient through a crossing uses a variable permutation or one divided difference, decreasing its order by at most one, so any finite product has a uniform finite order loss. The displayed completed PBW expansion is therefore the actual central completion, rather than an additional relation imposed on $R_\beta$. [step 1.1, step 10.1, algebra]

12.1 The common degenerate Hecke operator. In the fraction algebra set $Z_r=x_r-x_{r+1}$ and $S_r=(1+Z_r^{-1})\sigma_r-Z_r^{-1}$. On an unequal source component the diagonal term is $-z^{-1}f$, while its crossing coefficient on the target component is $1+(b-a+u-v)^{-1}$. On equal colors this operator is $\sigma_r-(1-\sigma_r)/(u-v)$ and preserves formal series. Thus $S_r$ acts on $\mathcal B_\beta$ in every case. All identities in the next two steps are computed in the fraction algebra and then hold for these regular operators. This use of auxiliary fractions does not assert that a dot difference is invertible in the completion or its quotients. [step 11.1, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

13.1 Hecke quadratic and mixed identities. Let $A=Z_r^{-1}$; then $\sigma_r(A)=-A$. Expanding $S_r^2$ gives identity coefficient $(1+A)(1-A)+A^2=1$ and crossing coefficient $(1+A)A-A(1+A)=0$. Thus $S_r^2=1$, including equal colors. In $S_rx_{r+1}-x_rS_r$ the crossing terms cancel and the diagonal term is $A(x_r-x_{r+1})=1$. Disjoint $S_r$ commute, and dots outside the pair commute with $S_r$. These are precisely the quadratic, mixed and far-commuting relations of [F2]. [F2, step 12.1, algebra]

14.1 Complete Hecke braid coefficients. In spectral variables put $Z=x_1-x_2$, $U=x_2-x_3$, $V=Z+U$, $A=Z^{-1}$, $B=U^{-1}$, $C=V^{-1}$. Both products $S_1S_2S_1$ and $S_2S_1S_2$ have coefficients, in permutation order $(1,s,t,st,ts,\rho)$, equal to $(-C-ABC,\ (1+A)BC,\ (1+B)AC,\ -B(1+A)(1+C),\ -A(1+B)(1+C),\ (1+A)(1+B)(1+C))$. To verify the reductions, multiply using $(f\sigma)(g\eta)=f\sigma(g)\sigma\eta$, $s(A)=-A$, $s(B)=C$, $t(B)=-B$, $t(A)=C$, and $AB=C(A+B)$. For example the raw $s$ coefficient in the first word is $A(1+A)(B-C)=(1+A)BC$; its raw identity coefficient is $-(1-A^2)C-A^2B=-C-ABC$. Interchanging $A,B$ and $s,t$ gives the second word's identical six coefficients. [step 13.1, step 12.1, algebra]

15.1 All five reverse braid cases. Step 14.1 is a rational identity in independent spectral variables, before assigning colors. Substitute $(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(a+u,b+v,c+w)$ on each source component and apply the color-permuting operators. It proves the full Hecke braid separately on $(a,b,c)$ with all distinct, $(a,a,b)$, $(a,b,b)$, $(a,b,a)$ and $(a,a,a)$, because each is the restriction of the same six-coefficient identity and every $S_r$ preserves $\mathcal B_\beta$ by step 12.1. Even when a displayed spectral denominator has zero constant, cancellation occurs in the original regular operators, and injectivity into fractions preserves the equality. Thus the all-equal reverse case also has a complete coefficient computation. [step 12.1, step 14.1, algebra]

16.1 Faithfulness for the Hecke action. The mixed relation moves polynomials to the right of $s$-words and the exact symmetric-group relations reduce each word to $s_w$, so $H_n^{\mathrm{dg}}$ is spanned by $s_wf(x)$. In the action of steps 12.1–15.1 its leading permutation coefficient is the product of nonzero rational factors $1+Z^{-1}$ along a reduced word. All lower terms have shorter permutation length. The shortest-relation argument of step 10.1 proves independence and therefore the affine Hecke PBW basis. Completing at the central ideal of step 1.1 gives the finite coefficientwise PBW module $\sum_{w,\nu}s_w k[\![y]\!]e(\nu)$; its operator action remains faithful by the same argument over formal fractions. The coefficients $1+Z^{-1}$ need only be nonzero in that field, not units in the coefficient ring. [F2, step 1.1, step 10.1, step 13.1, step 15.1, algebra]

17.1 Comparing the explicit tables. On an unequal source $(a,b)$, $S_r+p_{ab}$ has only the crossing term. Its target coefficient is $1+\zeta^{-1}$, where $\zeta=b-a+u-v$. Right multiplication by $q_{ab}^{-1}$ substitutes $(v,u)$ on that target. If $a\to b$, $q_{ab}(v,u)=1+\zeta^{-1}$, giving coefficient $1$; if $a\leftarrow b$, $q_{ab}(v,u)=-\zeta^{-1}$ and $\zeta=-1+u-v$, giving coefficient $-(\zeta+1)=v-u$; off edges the quotient is again $1$. On equal colors $S_r=\sigma_r-(1-\sigma_r)/(u-v)$, and $(S_r+1)(1+v-u)^{-1}=(\sigma_r-1)/(u-v)=E_r$ by moving the inverse through $\sigma_r$. Thus $(S_r+p)q^{-1}=\psi_r$ in the faithful action. Equivalently $\psi_rq-p=S_r$. [step 16.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 12.1, algebra]

18.1 Homomorphisms in both directions. Faithfulness in steps 10.1–11.1 and 16.1 transfers the concrete equalities to the completed presented algebras. Step 17.1 identifies the forward images with the operators checked in steps 4.1–9.1, so all KLR relations hold in $\widehat H_\beta^{\mathrm{dg}}$. It identifies the reverse images with the operators checked in steps 13.1–15.1, so all Hecke relations hold in $\widehat R_\beta$. The coefficient-algebra maps identify the central completion topologies: the symmetric ideal vanishing at the spectral multiset and the all-zero dot ideal have cofinal powers on $\mathcal B_\beta$ by step 1.1. Therefore the maps extend continuously to the stated completions. This proves both directions locally rather than importing a cyclic finite-$e$ theorem. [step 1.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 8.1, step 9.1, step 11.1, step 13.1, step 15.1, step 16.1, step 17.1, construct]

19.1 Inverse composites and uniformity. The coefficient maps fix every $e(\nu)$ and invert $y_r=x_r-\nu_r$ componentwise. The crossing composites are $(\psi_rq-p+p)q^{-1}=\psi_r$ and $((s_r+p)q^{-1})q-p=s_r$, with the same right multiplication order. Hence each composite is the identity on its generators, coefficient series and completion. None of $p,q,c$ depends on the rank, multiset, interval endpoints, level or cyclotomic charge, so enlarging an interval preserves every formula on the old tuples. Nilpotent dots permit finite evaluation of series, and every proved identity survives a quotient. Rank zero has coefficient algebra $k$ and both maps are the identity; empty positive-rank sectors have zero algebra. No assertion about cyclotomic support, based Grothendieck classes or Specht modules is needed for this local comparison. [step 18.1, algebra] ∎

item.title: Generic nondegenerate local inverse tables on integer colors
item.statement:
Work over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, with $q\in k^\times$ of infinite multiplicative order, integer colors, and the arrows $a\to a+1$. On any finite permutation-stable set of color words, complete the dot ring at the zero dots. The completed local affine Hecke presentation at spectral words $(q^{i_1},\ldots,q^{i_d})$ and the completed type-$A_\infty$ KLR presentation have mutually inverse changes of generators below. This is a local statement; it does not assert cyclotomic support, a tower comparison, or a Specht dictionary.

Write $x=q^a(1-u)$, $z=q^b(1-v)$ and set
$$P_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1&a=b,\\(1-q)/(1-x/z)&a\ne b,\end{cases}$$
$$Q_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1-q+qv-u&a=b,\\-q^a/(x-z)&a=b+1,\\(x-qz)/(x-z)&a\ne b,\ a\ne b+1.\end{cases}$$
These are explicit, invertible, rank-independent power series over $k$; in particular the result applies over $\mathbb C$. Use $y_r=1-q^{-i_r}X_r$ on $e(i)$ and the source convention $\psi_r=-\tau_r$, where $\tau$ is the native crossing. The changes of generators are
$$\psi_re(i)=(T_r+P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))Q_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})^{-1}e(i),$$
$$X_re(i)=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i),\qquad T_re(i)=(\psi_rQ_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})-P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))e(i).$$
The quadratic polynomial is $K_{aa}=0$, $K_{a,a+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $K_{a+1,a}(u,v)=u-v$, and $K_{ab}=1$ otherwise. Equal-color dot-sliding constants for $\psi$ are $+1$. The braid order is $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1-\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$; on $(a,b,a)$ its value is $[K_{ab}(u,v)-K_{ab}(w,v)]/(w-u)$, hence respectively $+1,-1,0$ for forward, backward, nonadjacent colors.
item.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The integer-color local presentations just stated. Their coefficient ring is the direct sum of one formal power-series ring per color word; no finite-$e$ definition or comparison theorem is being instantiated. In the Hecke presentation the spectral idempotents are the projections to these local rings. Multiplication by $X_r$ on its $i$-summand is $q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$. The usual affine Hecke relations are $T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q$, $T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1}$, and the braid and distant commutation relations.

## Proof

**Given:** The displayed presentations and the formal series $P,Q$.

1.1 All coefficients are legal. For $a\ne b$, $x-z$ has constant $q^a-q^b\ne0$. In the last case of $Q$, $x-qz$ has nonzero constant because $a\ne b+1$. In the backward case $-q^a/(x-z)$ is a unit. In the equal case $1-q\ne0$. Thus every denominator is a unit and each $Q$ is a unit. The formulas depend only on the adjacent pair, so they make sense in every rank and in every finite color window. [given, algebra]



1.2 Use an explicit polynomial representation. On the $i$-component let dots multiply, and let a permutation simultaneously permute coordinates and colors. With $\partial_r=(s_r-1)/(y_r-y_{r+1})$, define $\psi_r$ on an equal pair to be $\partial_r$; on an unequal source pair $(a,b)$ let its output in the swapped component be $h_{ab}(u,v)s_r$, where $h_{ab}(u,v)=v-u$ if $a=b+1$ and $h_{ab}=1$ otherwise. The equal-color quotient is a power series because the numerator vanishes on $u=v$. Its product rule is $\partial(fg)=\partial(f)g+(sf)\partial(g)$. Consequently $\partial v=u\partial+1$, $v\partial=\partial u+1$, and $\partial^2=0$. On unequal pairs the square is multiplication by $h_{ba}(u,v)h_{ab}(v,u)=K_{ab}(u,v)$. These computations verify all mixed and quadratic relations, including the native sign $\tau=-\psi$. [given, algebra]



2.1 Three distinct colors. In both three-crossing words the coefficient of the longest permutation is the product of the three pair factors, transported to the same coordinates. Each pair is crossed once. The factors commute and $s_1s_2s_1=s_2s_1s_2$, so the two words agree. This argument does not require nonadjacency; some of the factors can be linear. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.2 First two colors equal. For $(a,a,b)$ write $h=h_{ab}$. The left word is $h(u,v)h(u,w)s_1s_2\partial_1$, and the right word is $\partial_2h(u,v)h(u,w)s_1s_2$. The product of factors is invariant under swapping $v,w$, so its $\partial_2$ is zero. Also $\partial_2s_1s_2=s_1s_2\partial_1$ by conjugating the displayed quotient. The words agree. For $(a,b,b)$ the left word is $\partial_1h(v,w)h(u,w)s_2s_1$, and the right word is $h(v,w)h(u,w)s_2s_1\partial_2$. Here the product is invariant under swapping $u,v$, and $\partial_1s_2s_1=s_2s_1\partial_2$. This verifies the third color pattern separately. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.3 Outer colors equal. On $(a,b,a)$ with $a\ne b$, put $h=h_{ab}$ and $g=h_{ba}$. Expanding the one equal-color crossing gives left and right words $\frac{g(u,v)}{u-w}\bigl(h(v,w)s_1s_2s_1-h(v,u)\bigr),\qquad\frac{h(v,w)}{u-w}\bigl(g(u,v)s_2s_1s_2-g(w,v)\bigr).$ Their longest-permutation terms cancel. Their difference is $[K_{ab}(w,v)-K_{ab}(u,v)]/(u-w)$, the stated braid correction. This equals $1$ when $b=a+1$, $-1$ when $a=b+1$, and zero otherwise. Thus the apparent denominator cancels identically. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.4 All three colors equal. Put $D=(u-v)(u-w)(v-w)$. Expanding the quotients and collecting each of the six permutations gives $\partial_1\partial_2\partial_1=\partial_2\partial_1\partial_2=-D^{-1}\sum_{t\in S_3}\operatorname{sgn}(t)t.$ The numerator is alternating and hence divisible by each of the three pair differences, so this is an operator on power series. This explicitly supplies the all-equal case omitted as an exercise in the source. Together with steps 2.1–2.3 it proves all five braid patterns. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.5 Compute the Hecke generators in the same representation. At an output component set $U=X_r$, $V=X_{r+1}$. For unequal colors the swapped input series $Q$ times $h$ is $(qU-V)/(U-V)$: in the backward case $qU-V=q^a(v-u)$, and the swapped input series is $-q^a/(V-U)=q^a/(U-V)$, so multiplying by $h=v-u$ gives exactly the stated coefficient. In every other unequal case this is the last row of $Q$ directly. Also $-P=(1-q)V/(U-V)$. For equal colors, expand $\partial Q-1$; its permutation coefficient is $(1-q+qu-v)/(u-v)$ and its identity coefficient is $-(1-q)(1-v)/(u-v)$. Thus in every case $T_r=A(U,V)s_r+B(U,V),\qquad A(U,V)=\frac{qU-V}{U-V},\quad B(U,V)=\frac{(1-q)V}{U-V}.$ The equal-color poles cancel on power series, as follows already from $T=\partial Q-1$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]



3.1 Mixed and quadratic Hecke identities. Write $A_{ij}=A(X_i,X_j)$ and $B_{ij}=B(X_i,X_j)$. Direct common-denominator expansion gives $B_{ij}+B_{ji}=q-1$, $A_{ij}=q-B_{ij}$, and $A_{ij}A_{ji}=q+(q-1)B_{ij}-B_{ij}^2$. Squaring $A_{ij}s+B_{ij}$ therefore gives $(q-1)T+q$. The identity $TX_i-X_{i+1}T=(1-q)X_{i+1}$ follows by cancellation of its permutation term. Combining this identity with the quadratic identity gives $TX_iT=qX_{i+1}$. Distant commutations follow from disjoint variables. [step 2.5, algebra]



4.1 The Hecke braid holds in every color pattern, including all equal. Set $c=q-1$. Clearing the three pair denominators gives the rational identity $B_{13}(c-B_{12}-B_{23})+B_{12}B_{23}=0$. The coefficients of the longest permutation, $s_1s_2$, and $s_2s_1$ in $T_1T_2T_1$ are $A_{12}A_{13}A_{23}$, $A_{12}A_{13}B_{23}$, and $B_{12}A_{23}A_{13}$; the right word has the same coefficients. The $s_1$ coefficients are $A_{12}(B_{13}B_{21}+B_{12}B_{23})$ and $A_{12}B_{23}B_{13}$; the displayed identity makes them equal. The $s_2$ comparison is its transposed version. The identity coefficients differ by $(B_{12}-B_{23})\bigl(B_{13}(c-B_{12}-B_{23})+B_{12}B_{23}\bigr)=0.$ This uses the quadratic product identity of step 3.1. These are all six permutations, so the braid is proved. It is a rational identity before any color specialization; the equal-color operators preserve power series by step 2.5. [step 2.5, step 3.1, algebra]



5.1 These operator checks imply presentation identities, rather than identities on a possibly nonfaithful module. For Hecke coefficients the relation is $T_rf=(s_rf)T_r+B(X_r,X_{r+1})(f-s_rf)$. It follows first on the Laurent generators from the affine mixed relation, then on products by its product rule, and on formal local coefficients by continuity. At equal colors $f-s_rf$ is divisible by $X_r-X_{r+1}$; at unequal colors that denominator is a unit. This also gives the spectral-idempotent relation by applying the same formula to the local projections. For KLR use its displayed divided-difference product rule. Thus in either presentation coefficients can be moved past crossings. A crossing word reduces to a chosen reduced word for a permutation: delete adjacent repeated simple reflections using the quadratic relation, and change reduced words using commuting and three-term braid moves. For KLR the braid correction has fewer crossings. Induction on crossing length therefore spans the algebra by coefficient multiples of one chosen word per permutation. The elementary adjacent-transposition sorting algorithm supplies the requisite Coxeter reductions. In the rational crossed-product action, each reduced word has a nonzero coefficient of its own permutation; all other terms have shorter permutation length. Distinct permutations are linearly independent over the rational function field: in a minimal nonzero relation of automorphisms, apply it to $fg$ and subtract one automorphism's value on $f$ times its application to $g$; choose a coordinate $f$ moved differently by two permutations to obtain a shorter relation, a contradiction. Color words in different output components are already independent. Hence the spanning words are independent and both actions are faithful. The argument extends to formal coefficients using their fraction fields and the same finite spanning words. [step 1.2, step 2.4, step 4.1, algebra]



6.1 Both directions and both composites. In the faithful KLR action, steps 2.5–4.1 prove the Hecke relations of the displayed inverse generators. In the faithful local Hecke action, solving step 2.5 gives precisely the polynomial crossings of step 1.2, whose relations were proved in steps 1.2 and 2.1–2.4. Since $Q$ is a unit, the two operator subalgebras generated by coefficients and their respective crossings coincide. Thus the presentations are isomorphic. On idempotents and dots the two composites are the identity by the spectral decomposition and $X_r=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$. On crossings the composite is $(\psi_rQ-P+P)Q^{-1}=\psi_r$; on Hecke crossings it is $(T_r+P)Q^{-1}Q-P=T_r$. These are ordered products; no coefficient has been commuted past a crossing. This completes the local inverse comparison in both directions. [step 1.1, step 5.1, construct] ∎

item.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The parameters, presentations, and the following two explicit
conditional inputs.

[A1] [[lem-generic-cyclotomic-type-a-support-is-bounded-by-rank]] supplies the support input: the algebras in rank $d>0$ are finite-dimensional, their dots are
nilpotent, and every surviving color lies in
$B_d=[\min S-d+1,\max S+d-1]\cap\mathbb Z$. Hecke joint spectral
projectors $e_H(\nu)$ exist over $k$, with eigenvalues $\nu_r$ or
$\xi^{\nu_r}$. The full-line KLR rank algebra is unchanged by any finite
interval containing $B_d$. At level zero all positive ranks are zero and
rank zero is $k$.

[A2] There are fixed pairwise formal series $p_{ab},q_{ab},P_{ab},Q_{ab}$
for every $a,b\in\mathbb Z$, independent of rank, multicharge, content and
window; $q_{ab},Q_{ab}$ are units. On every finite integer window, the local
replacements displayed in the Statement satisfy all affine mixed,
quadratic, distant and braid relations in both directions, with the same
KLR convention. This input is supplied locally by
[[lem-integer-color-degenerate-hecke-klr-local-inverse-tables]] and
[[lem-generic-nondegenerate-local-inverse-tables]], including all five equality
patterns of three colors in the same native convention $\psi=-\tau$; the
cited article and a finite-$e$ instantiation do not replace these local proofs. The first direction
uses the actual Hecke joint projectors and dots; the reverse uses the KLR
word idempotents and dots. No cyclotomic relation, inverse composite,
spectral identification or tower assertion is assumed in this input.

## Proof

1.1 Evaluate a formal series in commuting nilpotent dots by its finite Taylor sum. This evaluation is independent of the nilpotence exponent chosen: every larger truncation differs only by zero monomials. A series with nonzero constant term is a unit by a terminating geometric expansion. Thus all replacements in the Statement are defined. By [A1] only finitely many words survive in any rank. The local relation verifications in [A2], applied on those words, give homomorphisms between the affine presentations before checking the first-strand quotient. No cyclic wraparound or reduction of integer colors is used. [A1, A2, algebra]

2.1 On a first color $i$, write the degenerate cyclotomic polynomial as $f(i+y)=y^{\lambda_i}U_i(y)$, where $U_i(y)=\prod_{m_j\ne i}(i-m_j+y)$. Its constant term is nonzero in characteristic zero. In the other branch $g(\xi^i(1-y))=(-\xi^i)^{\lambda_i}y^{\lambda_i}V_i(y)$, where $V_i(y)=\prod_{m_j\ne i}(\xi^i-\xi^{m_j}-\xi^iy)$. Infinite multiplicative order makes its constant term nonzero. Both auxiliary factors are units after nilpotent evaluation. Thus the Hecke cyclotomic relation on each projector is equivalent to $y_1^{\lambda_i}e(i,\ldots)=0$. If $\lambda_i=0$, the unit polynomial kills the entire projector. This proves the cyclotomic factorization and descent in both directions. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Denote the descended reverse map by $\sigma_d:H_d\to R_d^\lambda$. On $e_R(\nu)R_d^\lambda$, each $\sigma_d(x_r)$ has sole generalized eigenvalue $\nu_r$, or $\sigma_d(X_r)$ has sole generalized eigenvalue $\xi^{\nu_r}$. Distinct colors have distinct values, and the orthogonal word idempotents sum to one. The simultaneous primary projector is therefore precisely left multiplication by $e_R(\nu)$. The Hecke polynomial projector maps to this idempotent: its Chinese-remainder polynomial is one modulo the corresponding primary factors and zero modulo all other factors. Hence $\sigma_d(e_H(\nu))=e_R(\nu)$. The forward map already sends $e_R(\nu)$ to $e_H(\nu)$. [A1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Both composites fix the word projectors by step 3.1 and the dots by direct substitution $x_r-\nu_r=y_r$, or $1-\xi^{-\nu_r}X_r=y_r$. On a word, the crossing composite is $(\psi_rq_{ab}-p_{ab}+p_{ab})q_{ab}^{-1}=\psi_r$, or $(\psi_rQ_{ab}-P_{ab}+P_{ab})Q_{ab}^{-1}=\psi_r$. Conversely the Hecke composite sends $s_re_H(\nu)$ to $((s_r+p_{ab})q_{ab}^{-1}q_{ab}-p_{ab})e_H(\nu)=s_re_H(\nu)$; the formula with $T,P,Q$ is identical. The polynomial generators are fixed, and the units $X_r^{-1}$ are fixed because inverses are unique. Thus the homomorphisms are inverse on every generator, without commuting a crossing through its series. [step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For ranks through $D>0$ at positive level use the common interval $W_D=[\min S-D,\max S+D]\cap\mathbb Z$. It contains the support through rank $D$ and one unused ghost color beyond each endpoint of $B_D$. A crossing permutes existing colors and never creates one; nevertheless these endpoint colors keep every boundary edge of a surviving color represented by the integer-line convention. For operations reaching rank $D+t$, use $W_{D+t}$, and enlarge further to contain any specified color and its neighbors. All extra word idempotents vanish by [A1]. Since [A2] fixes the same series for each ordered pair in every interval, evaluation on surviving words is unchanged by enlargement. The resulting maps are independent of windows and glue across all finite rank bounds. [A1, A2, step 4.1, construct]

6.1 Let $\iota_H:H_d\to H_{d+1}$ send each existing Hecke generator to the generator with the same index. It is a homomorphism because all rank-$d$ relations, including the first-strand relation, hold in rank $d+1$. Its spectral projector satisfies $\iota_H(e_H(\nu))=\sum_a e_H(\nu,a)$: the first $d$ polynomial generators give a representation of $H_d$ on the rank-$d+1$ regular module, so their primary projector is the sum of exactly these joint projectors. Prefixes violating rank-$d$ support are zero by [A1] applied to this representation. This argument also holds for $d=0$, where the empty projector is one. [A1, given, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Define $\iota_R=\sigma_{d+1}\iota_H\phi_d$. The established inverse maps make this a homomorphism. Steps 3.1 and 6.1 give $\iota_R(e_R(\nu))=\sum_a e_R(\nu,a)$. The unchanged polynomial generators give the usual prefix dots. For $r<d$, the rank-independent pair series in [A2] and cancellation in step 4.1 give $\iota_R(\psi_re_R(\nu))=\sum_a\psi_re_R(\nu,a)$. These are exactly the standard right-appending KLR maps, so the individually constructed isomorphisms commute with the actual tower maps. Injectivity of the tower maps is neither needed nor inferred. [A2, step 4.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 Put $\epsilon_i^R=\sum_\nu e_R(\nu,i)$ in rank $d+1$, and define $\epsilon_i^H$ by the analogous spectral sum. Step 3.1 gives $\phi_{d+1}(\epsilon_i^R)=\epsilon_i^H$. Each last-color projector commutes with every prefix generator, since prefix crossings permute only the first $d$ colors and prefix dots preserve all colors. On left modules color restriction is $N\mapsto\epsilon_iN$, with the rank-$d$ action through its prefix map. Color induction is $M\mapsto A_{d+1}\epsilon_i\otimes_{A_d}M$. Step 7.1 identifies both prefix actions, and the algebra isomorphism identifies these induction bimodules on both sides. Explicitly $a\epsilon_i\otimes m\mapsto\phi_{d+1}(a)\epsilon_i\otimes m$ is a balanced bijection, with inverse obtained from $\sigma_{d+1}$. Restriction agrees by the same projector equality. These formulas are natural in module maps. [step 3.1, step 7.1, construct]

9.1 Composing the two comparisons through the same $R_d^\lambda$ proves the claimed degenerate/nondegenerate tower equivalence. Naturality from step 8.1 intertwines repeated induction and restriction, while step 5.1 covers every specified finite rank cut. At level zero use the identity on rank zero and the unique maps between zero algebras in positive rank; the sole map from rank zero to rank one is the map to zero, and all positive-rank functors vanish. Thus all ranks and levels are included. Every conclusion remains conditional on [A1] and [A2]; no local table identity or based theorem has been established by this gluing proof. [A1, step 5.1, step 8.1] ∎

item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N(\mathbb C)$,
with upper-triangular Borel, and represent $a=\lambda+\rho$ by coordinates
of sum zero. For every $i<j$ with $a_i-a_j\in\mathbb Z$, require
$a_i-a_j\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$. Thus $a$ is regular and strictly decreasing
inside each coordinate coset modulo $\mathbb Z$; there is no ordering of
complex numbers from different cosets. Write $P$ for the weight lattice,
$U_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\lambda$, and
$\mathcal O_{\lambda+P}$ for objects of genuine $\mathcal O$ whose weights
belong to $\lambda+P$.

Let $\mathcal H_\chi$ consist of finitely generated $U$-bimodules $B$ with
$B\ker\chi_\lambda=0$ and locally finite adjoint $\mathfrak g$-action.
For finite-dimensional $E$ let $\Phi_E=E\otimes U_\chi$, with diagonal
left action and ordinary right action. Then
$$T_\lambda(B)=B\otimes_U\Delta(\lambda)$$
is an exact equivalence $\mathcal H_\chi\simeq\mathcal O_{\lambda+P}$.
Every object on either side has a finite presentation by the respective
projective generators $\Phi_E$ and $E\otimes\Delta(\lambda)$. The induced
map is the natural, composition-preserving identification
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal H_\chi}(\Phi_E,\Phi_F)\ \cong\ (E^*\otimes F\otimes U_\chi)^{\mathfrak g}\ \cong\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E\otimes\Delta(\lambda),F\otimes\Delta(\lambda)).$$
The comparison commutes naturally with finite-dimensional tensoring.

For $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ the corresponding statement uses
$\mathcal O_{\lambda+\mathbb Z^N}$ and finite-dimensional modules with
integral coordinate weights; $\mathcal H_\chi$ additionally requires its
adjoint Cartan weights to be integral and its adjoint scalar centre to act
semisimply. No assertion here supplies standard-label transport, a
parabolic restriction, or this equivalence for a nonprojective source
Verma or a singular source weight.
item.strategy: Direct local proof: projectivity at regular coset-dominant lambda, norm and linkage control of tensor flags, finite tensor projective presentations on both sides, Duflo action identification of generator Hom spaces, then cokernel/kernel presentation comparison and the integral-coordinate gl_N centre extension.

item.title: Separated integral cosets give typed parabolic category equivalences
item.statement:
Assume AC. Work in genuine type-$A$ parabolic category $\mathcal O$ for
$\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its fixed Borel. Its column Levi has ordered
blocks of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. All entries in column $j$ lie in
$c_j+\mathbb Z$, where the original admissibility condition is
$c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z\Rightarrow c_j=c_k$. Use the source highest-weight
convention $\eta_i=a_i+i-1$ and half-sum
$\rho_i=(N+1-2i)/2$, with the column reading prescribed by the source Borel.
For each occurring entry coset $\kappa$ retain its columns in their original
order. Fix an order on the finite set of cosets; no order on $\mathbb C$ is used.

Subject to the local HC tensor-projective comparison stated in [F1], stable
sorting of the coordinates by $\kappa$ gives an exact, complex-linear
equivalence of the genuine parabolic categories, carrying each ordinary
Verma label by the dot permutation and carrying the corresponding generalized
standard, simple head and projective cover. On each linkage block, the sorted
category is equivalent to the product of the corresponding parabolic blocks
for $\mathfrak{gl}_{N_\kappa}$, where
$N_\kappa=\sum_{j\in\kappa}q_j$. Product means the abelian category generated
by finite presentations of outer tensor products, equivalently modules over
the tensor product of the finite block endomorphism algebras.

For the original pyramid with $n$ rows put $n_\kappa=\max_{j\in\kappa}q_j$.
The component integral entry dictionary is exactly
$$a_i^{\mathrm{int}}=a_i-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa,\qquad m_j=q_j-n_\kappa,\qquad \inf I_\kappa=1-n_\kappa.$$
Thus $m_j+1-\inf I_\kappa=q_j$, with the original nonincreasing retained
heights and charges. For the admitted-ground subcategories, where each original entry has a
nonnegative integral difference from its own ground entry, this dictionary
lands in the bounded-below admitted integral component models of [F4]. For
other genuine parabolic blocks it records the integral weight/coset
dictionary and the trace shift, without asserting membership in that fixed
admitted cut. If the component follows $B_\kappa$ sorted coordinates, its
Levi highest weight and the integral highest weight differ by the scalar
trace-character shift
$$\delta_\kappa=B_\kappa+c_\kappa-n+n_\kappa.$$
This shift is a Lie algebra character and requires no integrality of
$c_\kappa$. Singular repeated-entry linkage blocks are included. The original
complex origins, component entry multisets and their scalar centres remain
recorded; different complex cosets are not merged into one integral block.

Sorting commutes coherently with finite tensoring and its invariant Casimir
and permutation maps. The separated product decomposition is blockwise and
does not assert that unrestricted tensoring is componentwise. The proof gives
its actual filtration and block-projection comparison. Choices of sorting
word with the same stable permutation yield the natural comparison fixed on
the chosen reference highest vector and its tensor-projective presentations.
item.strategy: Sixteen-step local direct proof: exact Ore quotient and normalized different-coset Verma transport; tensor-projective Hom comparison; parabolic Serre restriction; top-centre/radical-invariant PBW induction equivalence; outer tensor projective presentations; scalar trace shifts; projected tensor filtrations and Casimir dictionary. Fixed admitted integral cut used only under admitted-ground hypothesis.

before.title: The projective Grothendieck group is the integral highest weight module
before.statement:
For the standard homogeneous graded quotient over any field, with arbitrary real symmetrizable Cartan datum and admissible graded KLR parameters, there is a unique $U_A$-module isomorphism $\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ sending $1_\Lambda$ to $v_\Lambda$ and intertwining all normalized $E_i,F_i,K_i$ and divided powers. In particular $K_0$ is free over $A$. On the NEGATIVE half the vacuum map has exact kernel
$$\ker(U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda))=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda_i}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}.$$
This is the integral negative-half presentation; neither a full-$U_A$ quotient by only $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$ nor invertibility of divided-power factorials is asserted.
For projectives, the tensor form $T(P,Q)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes Q)$ transports to the highest-weight contravariant form normalized by $(v_\Lambda,v_\Lambda)=1$ and $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$, $\sigma(K_i)=K_i$. It is not the generic negative-half Lusztig form with a newly alleged radical.
before.strategy:
1. Divided-word vacuum generation is the preceding lemma. The finite-string lemma gives $F_i^{(s)}1_\Lambda=0$ for every $s>\lambda_i$, since the pure $i$ block then vanishes. Hence the vacuum map factors through the integral negative-half highest-weight quotient with the entire displayed family of divided powers. Use the existing highest-weight integral presentation, not multiplication by a nonunit quantum factorial.
2. Tensor with $\mathbb Q(q)$. The independent normalized-action supplier makes the target integrable, and it is generated by its nonzero highest vector. The simple integrable highest-weight uniqueness theorem identifies this rational cyclic module with $V(\Lambda)$. Thus the factored surjection $V_A(\Lambda)\to K_0$ is a rational isomorphism.
3. $V_A$ is torsion-free as its actual lattice in $V(\Lambda)$. The kernel of the integral surjection vanishes after localization, so each kernel element is torsion, hence zero. This proves the integral isomorphism; the normalized projective-cover shift orbits independently give the free $A$-basis. All divided and positive generators agree after rationalization, and torsion-freeness makes those operator equalities integral. This proves the kernel exactly, without an equal-rank heuristic over a nonfield.
4. The anti-involution flips tensor factors and gives symmetry of $T(P,Q)$. The basic corner tensor identities in the action theorem give $T(F_iP,Q)=T(P,E_i^{\rm basic}Q)$ and $T(E_i^{\rm basic}P,Q)=T(P,F_iQ)$. On a target root $\beta$, $q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$ equals $E_i^{\rm basic}$, and the other formula gives the stated $\sigma(E_i)$ after the weight shift. The vacuum form is $1$. Cyclic generation and the contravariant-form uniqueness supplier therefore identify this form with the actual highest-weight form. No negative-half radical argument enters.

before.title: Cyclotomic KLR quotients in ranks zero, one and two
before.statement:
Work over any field $k$ with a real symmetrizable Cartan datum, arbitrary symmetrizers $d_i$, dominant $\Lambda$ and the STANDARD homogeneous polynomials $a_i=u^{\lambda_i}$.
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$ has one normalized simple and projective, the vacuum.
(b) For every color $i$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg x=2d_i$ and graded dimension $\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}q^{2d_ir}$ when $\lambda_i\ge1$. Its unique normalized simple is $k$, its normalized projective HOM-self-dual cover is the regular module, and the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda_i-1}$ Frobenius FUNCTIONAL has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. If $\lambda_i=0$ the block is zero and has NO simple; if $\lambda_i=1$ it is $k$.
(c) In rank one $I=\{i\}$, at EVERY $n\ge0$ the algebra is the cyclotomic nil-Hecke quotient $NH_n/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$. It is nonzero precisely for $0\le n\le\lambda_i$. At each such root it has exactly one normalized self-dual simple, and zero blocks have none; hence there are $\lambda_i+1$ normalized simple classes in total, matching the rank-one highest-weight module. For $1\le n\le\lambda_i$ its symmetric corner is $k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]/(h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i})$, the graded Grassmannian coinvariant ring, and the algebra is the associated graded polynomial-column matrix algebra. The normalized simple column has graded dimension $[n]_{q_i}!$, where $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
(d) Explicitly at $\lambda_i=2,n=2$, the block is $\operatorname{End}_k(C\{-d_i\})$ with $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$, its basis $1,x_1$ in degrees $0,2d_i$. Its unique self-dual simple $S_2=C\{-d_i\}$ has graded dimension $q_i^{-1}+q_i$ and is also the normalized indecomposable projective $P_2$. It is NOT a one-dimensional module with both dots zero. The regular class is $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=[2]_{q_i}[P_2]$ in $K_0$ and $[2]_{q_i}[S_2]$ in $G_0$.
(e) Arbitrary monic $a_i$ gives the ungraded deformation: $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$. Ordinary finiteness/symmetry remain true, but this is not the standard graded $V(2)$ identification.
before.strategy:
1. At rank zero use the convention in the definition. At one strand there are no crossings, so the presentation gives exactly the displayed truncated polynomial ring and homogeneous monomial basis. For positive $\lambda_i$ the unique graded simple is its degree-zero quotient and evaluation identifies the regular cover's projective Hom dual with itself. At $\lambda_i=0$, $1=0$ and there is no simple. The nonzero trace input is in degree $2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$ and its output in degree zero, giving the NEGATIVE functional degree; the anti-diagonal monomial pairing proves perfectness over every field.
2. The explicit nil-Hecke endomorphism supplier gives $NH_n=\operatorname{End}_{S_n}(P_n)$ with $S_n=k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]$, $P_n=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. To compute the first-power ideal, use the finite free intermediate algebra $C_n=S_n[z]/(z^n-e_1z^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^ne_n)$, embedded by $z=x_1$. Polynomial division of $\prod_a(t-x_a)$ by $t-x_1$ identifies $C_n$ with $k[x_1,e'_1,\ldots,e'_{n-1}]$ for the remaining variables. Their Artin basis makes $P_n$ free of rank $(n-1)!$ over $C_n$. Thus multiplication by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$ is repeated multiplication by $z^{\lambda_i}$ on the $S_n$-basis $1,z,\ldots,z^{n-1}$. The two-sided matrix ideal it generates is the matrix ideal of its entries.
Use the coefficient trace $\epsilon(z^{n-1})=1$, $\epsilon(z^a)=0$ for $a<n-1$. The power-basis trace matrix is anti-triangular with unit anti-diagonal, so its dual basis is integral over $S_n$. Its recurrence from the displayed monic equation gives $\epsilon(z^{n-1+r})=h_r$. Accordingly the ideal of multiplication entries equals the ideal of all $\epsilon(z^{\lambda_i+a+b})=h_{\lambda_i+a+b-n+1}$ for $0\le a,b<n$, taking $h_r=0$ for $r<0$ and $h_0=1$. The order-$n$ recurrence expresses all indices above $\lambda_i$ in the first consecutive $n$ entries $h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i}$, giving exactly the stated corner ideal. For $n>\lambda_i$ it contains $h_0=1$; for $n\le\lambda_i$ all these generators have positive degree and the ideal lies in the augmentation ideal, so its quotient is NONZERO. It is finite by the independently proved finite-block supplier and the matrix corner, with degree-zero part $k$ and nilpotent positive-degree ideal. It consequently has one normalized graded simple. No Schur-basis or unproved Grassmannian-cohomology identification is needed.
3. The actual nil-Hecke matrix equivalence therefore gives exactly one simple column for every nonzero block. Its augmentation column is the ordinary $S_n$ coinvariant polynomial representation, with its Artin monomial basis and centering shift $-d_i\binom n2$. Its graded dimension is $q_i^{-\binom n2}\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})=[n]_{q_i}!$. The generic divided-power/normalized-simple supplier identifies this column as self-dual; quotient inflation preserves that normalization. Together with the rank-zero class, this gives precisely $\lambda_i+1$ classes, not a conclusion based solely on comparing a module dimension.
4. At $n=\lambda_i=2$ the symmetric corner is $k$. The column is the stated two-dimensional coinvariant module; $x_2=-x_1$, $x_1^2=0$, and multiplication/divided difference give the matrix units even in characteristic two. The regular endomorphism algebra is the column tensored with its vector dual, yielding the two shifts $\pm d_i$ and preserving the exact $[2]_{q_i}$ regular multiplicity. A one-dimensional zero-dot proposal violates the native equal-color mixed relation and is impossible. At $\lambda_i=1,n=2$ one can also see vanishing directly: from $x_1=0$ the actual native mixed equations give $x_2\tau=-1$ and $\tau x_2=-1$; multiplying by $\tau$ and using $\tau^2=0$ gives $\tau=0$ and then $1=0$.
5. Finally the coprime monic factors $u,u-1$ give $k\oplus k$, with two ordinary simple classes. This proves the deformation boundary while retaining the full standard graded rank-one scope.

after.title: Cyclotomic KLR quotients in ranks zero, one and two
after.statement:
Work over any field $k$ with a real symmetrizable Cartan datum, arbitrary symmetrizers $d_i$, dominant $\Lambda$ and the STANDARD homogeneous polynomials $a_i=u^{\lambda_i}$.
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$ has one normalized simple and projective, the vacuum.
(b) For every color $i$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg x=2d_i$ and graded dimension $\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}q^{2d_ir}$ when $\lambda_i\ge1$. Its unique normalized simple is $k$, its normalized projective HOM-self-dual cover is the regular module, and the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda_i-1}$ Frobenius FUNCTIONAL has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. If $\lambda_i=0$ the block is zero and has NO simple; if $\lambda_i=1$ it is $k$.
(c) In rank one $I=\{i\}$, at EVERY $n\ge0$ the algebra is the cyclotomic nil-Hecke quotient $NH_n/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$. It is nonzero precisely for $0\le n\le\lambda_i$. At each such root it has exactly one normalized self-dual simple, and zero blocks have none; hence there are $\lambda_i+1$ normalized simple classes in total, matching the rank-one highest-weight module. For $1\le n\le\lambda_i$ its symmetric corner is $k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]/(h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i})$, the graded Grassmannian coinvariant ring, and the algebra is the associated graded polynomial-column matrix algebra. The normalized simple column has graded dimension $[n]_{q_i}!$, where $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
(d) Explicitly at $\lambda_i=2,n=2$, the block is $\operatorname{End}_k(C\{-d_i\})$ with $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$, its basis $1,x_1$ in degrees $0,2d_i$. Its unique self-dual simple $S_2=C\{-d_i\}$ has graded dimension $q_i^{-1}+q_i$ and is also the normalized indecomposable projective $P_2$. It is NOT a one-dimensional module with both dots zero. The regular class is $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=[2]_{q_i}[P_2]$ in $K_0$ and $[2]_{q_i}[S_2]$ in $G_0$.
(e) Arbitrary monic $a_i$ gives the ungraded deformation: $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$. Ordinary finiteness/symmetry remain true, but this is not the standard graded $V(2)$ identification.

before.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator in a small cyclotomic weight
before.statement:
Take $I=\{i\}$ with $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, $d_i=1$, $q_i=q$, and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$, so that $\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle=2$ and the standard cyclotomic quotient has relations $x_1^2e(\nu)=0$. Then:
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ with graded dimension $1+q^2$, and $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n\ge3$, so the functors on the nonzero weights are $F^\Lambda_i k=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i k=0$.
(b) The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-sl-two-categorical-commutator]] at $\beta=0$, $\lambda=\Lambda$ (case $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle=2\ge0$) reads $q^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus \mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}\cong E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$; on the vacuum it says $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i k\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$, which is exactly $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$.
(c) Consequently, with the normalized operators of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]], on $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda(0))]$: $E_iF_i[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ and $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=0$, so $[E_i,F_i][1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ with $K_i[1_\Lambda]=q^2[1_\Lambda]$; on $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda(0))]$ the same commutator identity holds: $F_i[k]=q^{-1}[k\oplus k\{2\}]$, $E_i$ lowers back, $F_iE_i[k]=0$, and $E_iF_i[k]=(q+q^{-1})[k]$. This is the mixed relation of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]] verified at the first nontrivial weight.
before.strategy: At $\lambda=2$ the rank-one nil-Hecke quotient calculation in [[ex-cyclotomic-klr-quotients-in-ranks-zero-one-and-two]] gives precisely the three nonzero blocks at roots $0,\alpha_i,2\alpha_i$, with higher blocks zero. Basic restriction of $F_i k=k[x]/x^2$ is the vector space $k\oplus k\{2\}$; restriction of the vacuum is zero. The actual categorical commutator at target weight $h=2$ has identity shifts $0,2$, so its vacuum evaluation is exactly this direct sum. Projective $E$ on input root $\alpha_i$ carries $q^{-1}$, yielding $q^{-1}(1+q^2)=q^{-1}+q$. The KK module $F$ from the vacuum also carries $q^{-1}$ while KK $E$ is raw, giving the same commutator. The canonical module action instead shifts $E$ and leaves $F$ raw, also giving the same result. All agree with $(q^2-q^{-2})/(q-q^{-1})$. The vanishing is the proved pure rank-one finite-string calculation, not a false propagation inference from a single higher-degree dot polynomial.

before.title: The projective-simple Cartan pairing in a small cyclotomic block
before.statement: For rank one $d_i=1$, $\lambda=2$, let $B_r=R^\Lambda(r\alpha_i)$. The normalized simples are $S_0=k$, $S_1=k$ with $x=0$, and $S_2=C\{-1\}$ of graded dimension $q^{-1}+q$, where $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$. Their normalized projective covers are $P_0=k$, $P_1=k[x]/x^2$, $P_2=S_2$. Then $T(P_r,S_s)=\delta_{rs}$, with distinct roots paired by zero. Under the integral projective identification $P_0,P_1,P_2$ map to $v,Fv,F^{(2)}v$, respectively, while $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[P_2]$ maps to $F^2v$. In $G_0$ the correct regular classes are $[B_1]=(1+q^2)[S_1]$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[S_2]$. The canonical restricted-dual map sends $S_r$ to the form-dual of the corresponding divided lower vector; it does not identify $B_1$ with $S_1$.
before.strategy: The preceding rank-one example supplies $B_1$ and the centered polynomial column for $B_2$. The first regular module has two composition factors $S_1,S_1\{2\}$, giving $1+q^2$. The second block is the endomorphism matrix algebra of the graded column $S_2$, so its regular left module is the column tensored with its graded vector dual: the latter has dimension $q+q^{-1}$, yielding the stated shifted-column decomposition in both groups. The normalized cover-to-head Hom space is $k$ in degree zero and there are no other simple types in a block; quotient-cover evaluation identifies its tensor pairing with this value. The divided-power idempotent identifies $P_2$ with the actual second divided induction, hence $[B_2]=[2]_q[P_2]$ and $F^2=[2]_qF^{(2)}$. This is a cover/simple pairing, not a Cartan matrix claimed to be all ones or a trace that removes a denominator. The integral and dual-module theorems give the stated two identifications.

before.title: Self-dual indecomposable KLR projectives give the lower global basis (symmetric type)
before.statement: Assume the Cartan datum of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] has symmetric Cartan matrix $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ and uses the quiver normalization $d_i=1$ for every i, the field $k$ has characteristic $0$, and the KLR parameters are the quiver-geometric ones (the specialization attached to a finite quiver without loops, with arbitrary arrow multiplicities $h_{ij}$ and $a_{ij}=-(h_{ij}+h_{ji})$: $Q_{ij}(u,v)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ for $i\ne j$, in the fixed native crossing-sign convention; arbitrary parameter changes, including a global replacement by $u+v$, require their own proved gauge equivalence). Then, normalizing each indecomposable finitely generated graded projective $R(\beta)$-module to be self-dual for the contravariant graded projective duality $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$ ($P\cong P^\#$ after the unique normalizing shift), the map $b\mapsto[P_b]$ is a bijection between the lower global basis $B(\infty)$ of the negative half ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) and the shift-orbit basis of $K_0(R)$ by self-dual indecomposable projectives; under the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] one has $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for the lower global lift $G(b)$, and the identification is compatible with the based quotient of [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]. No extension to arbitrary KLR parameters or to non-symmetric Cartan data is asserted here; any such extension requires its own parameter-change invariance theorem.
before.strategy:
Use the proved local quiver-flag semisimplicity corollary and signed Ext-realization theorem in the full finite loopless quiver scope, with arbitrary arrow multiplicities, normalized symmetric d_i=1 and any coefficient field k of characteristic zero. Put L_nu=R(pi_nu)!k[d_nu] and L=sum_nu L_nu. The semisimplicity corollary gives L as a finite direct sum of shifts of simple actual G-equivariant perverse objects. Its proof uses the explicit smooth projective finite-Borel compactification and one finite Stiefel model with r_N>=2f+dmax-dmin; the degree-zero End ring comparison uniquely lifts the finite orthogonal projectors, and bounded equivariant idempotent completeness plus normalized exact conservative perverse pullback reflects simple summands. This is actual equivariant semisimplicity, not an arbitrary nonequivariant splitting or an unproved purity import.
Identify the existing R(beta;Q) with the independently proved intrinsic signed algebra S_Gamma(beta) inside this argument. Take P_ij(u,v)=(v-u)^h_ij; then P_ij(u,v)P_ji(v,u)=Q_ij(u,v)=(-1)^h_ij(u-v)^(h_ij+h_ji). The original polynomial/PBW suppliers give the faithful native action with unequal crossing (x_r-x_(r+1))^h_ij s_r and equal crossing (1-s_r)/(x_r-x_(r+1)). Give the nu polynomial unit degree -d_nu and variables degree2. Since d_(s_r nu)-d_nu=h_ij-h_ji, an unequal crossing has degree2h_ij+d_nu-d_(s_r nu)=h_ij+h_ji=-a_ij; the equal crossing has degree-2. The intrinsic signed geometric supplier has precisely these faithful operators on the same shifted polynomial module, and its specified generators generate its algebra. Thus both faithful images are the same subalgebra of homogeneous endomorphisms generated by the identical projections, dots and crossings; their inverse image identifications give the unique graded R=S_Gamma isomorphism, without assuming a rank equality. Compose its proved genuine Ext/Borel-Moore product comparison to obtain R=Ext_G^*(L,L). Its source-first corners are e_nu R e_eta=Ext(L_nu,L_eta), and homogeneous product is a*b=b[n] composed with a. On Ext(L,T) this is exactly left precomposition. The selected equal geometric crossing is minus its standard complex BM class, while unequal crossings are the standard class; this keeps the native signs and never changes the ambient positive complex orientation.
With these two geometric suppliers and the preceding local comparison, the following finite graded-Yoneda argument applies. The graded Yoneda functor Y_T=Ext_G^*(delta L,T) gives a fully faithful equivalence from add(delta L shifts) to finite graded projective R-modules: verify it on the generator delta L by Hom_R(R,R)=R^op=End_DG(delta L) with ordinary categorical composition, extend to finite sums/shifts, and restrict to idempotent summands. Each simple perverse summand T belongs to that additive category after a shift. Therefore End_R^*(Y_T)=Ext_G^*(T,T). For perverse T the heart orthogonality gives Hom_DG(T,T[m])=0 for m<0, so this algebra has no negative degrees; its degree-zero part is the division algebra End(T). Thus Y_T is indecomposable. The same additive equivalence exhausts all indecomposable projective shift orbits. The algebraic maximal-tail supplier already proves every simple R-module absolutely simple; a division degree-zero endomorphism algebra of a projective cover injects into its simple-head scalar ring, so End_R^0(Y_T)=k. This proves the essential positive-End property without VV4.8 augmentation/formality and without relying on a generalized geometric canonical comparison.
By the separately proved generic projective-duality supplier every projective orbit has a unique #-self-dual representative P_b. Put x_b=gamma^-1[P_b]. It is integral and bar fixed. The exact Hom/tensor comparison for a self-dual P gives B_L(x_b,x_b)=h(P_b,P_b)=1+q N[[q]], since the geometric End property is unchanged by grading shifts. Dividing by C_beta=1 moduloq gives B_K(x_b,x_b) in1+q Z[[q]]. The general QG5 half norm criterion therefore places x_b in the q0 crystal lattice. Bar fixes it, so it also lies in the actual bar chart; integral balanced globalization writes x_b as a finite Z-linear combination of lower global vectors. Their residue Gram matrix is the identity; norm residue1 forces the sum of coefficient squares to be1. Thus x_b is exactly plus or minus one lower global vector. Distinct projective shift orbits are independent and have the same finite weight cardinality as the global basis by the integral K_0 isomorphism, so they exhaust this signed set.
The new positive divided-string leading-term supplier removes every minus sign using its integral LEFT-string ideal equality, coefficient1 projective adjunction and the general adapted LEFT global recursion from1. It retains the full symmetric claim and does not use batch8's finite-ADE canonical-comparison item. The based quotient then follows from the general QG5 zero/survival projection. This completes the local deduction from the declared geometric and algebraic suppliers; all of their actual proof contracts must be closed before this subject can be certified ready.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The symmetric quiver-normalized Cartan datum with $d_i=1$, a characteristic-zero field $k$, the quiver-geometric parameters $Q_{ij}(u,v)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$, the categorical form of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]], the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]], and the QG-5 global-basis machinery of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]], [[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]], [[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]], [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]].

**Choice.** Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice of the geometric and quantum suppliers; the finite presented-algebra comparison and finite graded Yoneda argument below introduce no additional choice.

[F1] Categorical input ([[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]]): $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras and twisted bialgebras intertwining the forms, and every finite graded projective has a normalized self-dual representative with the pairing of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]].

[F2] Positive first-string supplier ([[lem-klr-projective-duality-and-positive-divided-string-leading-terms]]): normalized self-dual projective covers satisfy the coefficient-$1$ FIRST-block expansion, the integral LEFT divided-string ideal equality, and the positive FIRST/LEFT global comparison; its inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is carried here.

[F3] Actual geometric realization ([[def-quiver-full-flag-incidence-varieties-and-geometric-klr-generators]], [[thm-signed-klr-algebra-is-the-equivariant-ext-algebra-of-quiver-flag-complexes]], [[thm-quiver-flag-convolution-generators-satisfy-the-signed-klr-relations]], [[thm-quiver-flag-relative-position-strata-give-a-faithful-geometric-pbw-basis]]): the intrinsic presentation has the full distinct-color adjacent dot slides, native equal-color mixed and braid signs, and a faithful action generated by the native polynomial operators on summands with unit degree $-d_\nu$; the Ext product is $a*b=b[n]\circ a$ for $a$ of degree $n$, with source-first corner $e_\eta R e_\nu=\operatorname{Ext}_G(L_\eta,L_\nu)$.

[F4] Actual semisimplicity ([[cor-quiver-full-flag-pushforwards-are-semisimple-in-characteristic-zero]]): for every finite loopless quiver with arbitrary finite arrow multiplicities and every characteristic-zero field, $L_\nu=R\pi_{\nu!}k[d_\nu]$ and their finite sum are finite direct sums of shifts of simple objects in the actual equivariant perverse heart of [[thm-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]]. That bounded heart gives $\operatorname{Hom}(T,T[n])=0$ for $n<0$ and division $\operatorname{End}(T)$ for simple $T$.

[F5] Projective covers ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]], [[lem-klr-maximal-tail-restriction-and-induction-have-a-unique-simple-head]]): graded indecomposable finite projectives are projective covers of finite-dimensional graded simples, and those simples are absolutely simple over $k$.


[F6] Actual splitting ([[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]): the bounded equivariant constructible category is triangulated and idempotent complete.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; build the geometric realization, run the graded-Yoneda argument, then globalize and fix the signs with the positive first-string supplier.

1.1 (The graded algebra comparison.) Set $P_{ij}(u,v)=(v-u)^{h_{ij}}$ for $i\ne j$. These are nonzero, including when $h_{ij}=0$, and $P_{ij}(u,v)P_{ji}(v,u)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}=Q_{ij}(u,v)$. Thus [[thm-polynomial-representation-of-a-klr-algebra]] gives a faithful action of $R(\beta;Q)$ by projections, dots and unequal crossings $(x_r-x_{r+1})^{h_{ij}}s_r$, with equal crossings $(1-s_r)/(x_r-x_{r+1})$. The actual geometric action of [F3] uses exactly those operators. In both actions give the unit of the $\nu$ polynomial summand degree $-d_\nu$: the incidence formula $d_\nu=\sum_i\beta_i(\beta_i-1)/2+\sum_{a>b}h_{\nu_a\nu_b}$ gives $d_{s_r\nu}-d_\nu=h_{ij}-h_{ji}$, so the unequal crossing has degree $2h_{ij}+d_\nu-d_{s_r\nu}=h_{ij}+h_{ji}$; equal crossings have degree $-2$ and dots degree $2$. Both faithful images are therefore the identical graded subalgebra generated by these operators, yielding $R(\beta;Q)\cong S_\Gamma(\beta)\cong\operatorname{Ext}_G^\bullet(L,L)$ for $L=\bigoplus_\nu L_\nu$. This is also the direct comparison of the identical specialized presentations: all adjacent unequal dot slides and the native mixed and braid signs are present in [F3]. The equal geometric crossing is minus its standard complex Borel–Moore class, so no sign change is implicit. [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 (The actual normalized complex.) By [F4], the same $L=\bigoplus_\nu R\pi_{\nu!}k[d_\nu]$ of step 1.1 is a finite direct sum of shifts of simple actual equivariant perverse objects. The normalization $[d_\nu]$ has already been included in $L_\nu$; no further shift of $L$ is made. This uses the proved semisimplicity clause in the complete loopless multiedge scope, with no semismallness or finite-ADE restriction. [F4, step 1.1]

2.2 (Graded Yoneda.) Use the shifted opposite-composition product of [F3] and define $Y_T=\operatorname{Ext}_G^\bullet(L,T)$ as a graded left $R$-module: for homogeneous $a:L\to L[n]$ and $y:L\to T[m]$, set $a\cdot y=y[n]\circ a$, so $(a*b)\cdot y=a\cdot(b\cdot y)$. On $T=L$ this is the regular left module. A homogeneous map $f:T\to U[t]$ acts by postcomposition $y\mapsto f[m]\circ y$ of degree $t$. For $T=U=L$ every graded $R$-linear map $R\to R$ is right multiplication by its value at $1$, hence is induced uniquely by the corresponding $f$; extend this identification to finite sums and shifts and then to idempotent summands. Since the actual category is idempotent complete and all finite graded projectives are summands of finite sums of shifts of $R$, this gives a fully faithful equivalence from the additive category generated by shifts of $L$ onto finite graded projectives, with $\operatorname{End}_R^\bullet(Y_T)\cong\operatorname{Ext}_G^\bullet(T,T)$ using ordinary categorical composition on both endomorphism rings. [F3, F6, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 (Indecomposables and scalar degree zero.) Each simple perverse summand $T$ in step 2.1 belongs to that additive category up to shift. By [F4] and step 2.2 its projective $Y_T$ has no negative-degree endomorphisms and its degree-zero endomorphism ring is a division algebra, hence it is graded indecomposable. These exhaust the indecomposable projective shift orbits: every projective is a summand of a finite sum of the $Y_T$ and their shifts, and [F5] gives the finite graded Krull–Schmidt decomposition. Distinct simple perverse objects yield distinct orbits, since full faithfulness would otherwise give $T\cong U[t]$, and perverse concentration forces $t=0$. Finally the simple head $S$ of $Y_T$ has $\operatorname{End}_R^0(S)=k$ by [F5]. Every degree-zero endomorphism preserves the unique maximal graded submodule, so descent to the head is a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $\operatorname{End}_R^0(Y_T)\to k$; its kernel is zero because its source is a division algebra, and its image contains all scalars, so $\operatorname{End}_R^0(Y_T)=k$. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]


4.1 (Self-dual normalization, norm one and signed globalization.) By [F1] every projective shift orbit has a unique $^\#$ self-dual representative $P_b$; put $x_b=\gamma^{-1}[P_b]$, which is integral and bar fixed. The exact Hom/tensor comparison for a self-dual $P$ gives $B_L(x_b,x_b)=h(P_b,P_b)$, a nonnegative integer power series in $q$ congruent to $1$ modulo $q$, since the geometric nonnegative-End property is unchanged by grading shifts. Dividing by $C_\beta$ (which is $1$ modulo $q$) gives a value $B_K(x_b,x_b)$ congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ with integer coefficients, so the general half norm criterion places $x_b$ in the $q^0$ crystal lattice; being bar fixed, it also lies in the actual bar chart, and the integral balanced globalization writes $x_b$ as a finite $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of lower global vectors. Their residue Gram matrix is the identity, so norm residue $1$ forces the sum of coefficient squares to be $1$: $x_b$ is exactly plus or minus one lower global vector. Distinct projective shift orbits are independent and have the same finite weight cardinality as the global basis by the integral $K_0$ isomorphism, so they exhaust this signed set. [step 3.1, F1, F2, algebra]

5.1 (Positivity and the based quotient.) The positive divided-string leading-term supplier [F2] removes every minus sign using its integral LEFT-string ideal equality, its coefficient-$1$ projective adjunction expansion, and the general adapted LEFT global recursion (carried with its inherited Axiom of Choice, [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); batch 8's finite-ADE canonical-comparison item is not used. Consequently the sign in step 4.1 is $+1$, giving $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for every lower global vector $G(b)$ and establishing the bijection of the statement. The compatibility with the based quotient is the general zero/survival projection theorem of the QG-5 machinery. [step 4.1, F2, algebra] ∎

before.title: Cyclotomic extension of scalars respects the based quotient (conditional)
before.statement:
Assume the full symmetric normalized-$d_i=1$, characteristic-zero, loopless-quiver geometric-parameter scope of the generic global theorem, and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient with RIGHT append. Let $\gamma:U_A^-\to K_0(R)$ be the approved generic categorification and $\phi:K_0(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ the vacuum-normalized integral isomorphism. Then the raw extension $q_\Lambda(P)=R^\Lambda\otimes_RP$ satisfies
$$\phi[q_\Lambda(P)]=\pi_\Lambda\bigl(*(\gamma^{-1}[P])\bigr).$$
Composing extension with the generic mirror twist gives $\pi_\Lambda$ without star. For $b\in B(\infty)$ and the generic normalized indecomposable projective $P_b$ with $\gamma^{-1}[P_b]=G^-(b)$, raw extension is zero or a SINGLE normalized indecomposable cyclotomic projective; its image is $\pi_\Lambda G^-(b^*)$, which is zero or $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda b^*)$. The surviving cover orbits do not merge, and every normalized cyclotomic cover is obtained. In RIGHT-simple labels $c$, the generic FIRST-recursion theorem gives $\gamma^{-1}[P(S_c)]=G^-(c^*)$, so raw extension sends it to $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda c)$; these are exactly the crystal-compatible survivor labels of the preceding theorem. The claim is for indecomposable projectives, not every finite projective quotient.
